text: Iterates matched feature retrieves associated annotated MS/MS spectra. Applies denoising multiple frequency thresholds (0.00 1.00 steps 0.01) generate subspectra. Stores thresholded spectra folder: Denoised_spectra_for_tuning/. feature: Matches thresholded spectra best-matching reference spectrum (identified denoising). Computes similarity scores using dot product-based metrics stores results After_denoising_matches/. Calculates: Signal reduction: Loss matching fragments post-denoising. Noise reduction: Reduction unmatched fragments (interpreted noise). FMR (Fragment Match Rate): Ratio matching total fragments denoising. Applies Pareto front analysis identify optimal trade-offs signal retention noise reduction. applicable, also uses knee-point detection differential evolution optimization (DEoptim) backup strategies. Stores results : CSV files evaluated matches (pareto_results/csv/) Pareto front plots feature (pareto_results/pdf/) Final optimal scores merged summary table. Calculates: percentage increase similarity scores (vs. denoising) Filters features improved scores positive signal retention downstream evaluation.

code: #This step reads in the mzML files, prepares the stats.txt file in a format that extracts MS2 spectra and returns a list folder_path = "~/metabolomics/test_1/" #folder path containing mzml/ and Stats.txt in required format l1 = preprocess(folder_path = folder_path, tol_mz = 5, tol_rt = 0.1) #reads mzml files, prepares Stats file, extracts spectra and concatenates spectra  #This step extracts the top 80% TIC spectra and groups fragments within a given mass tolerance l2 = extract_raw_spectra(folder_path = folder_path, l1, 0.05, 0.8) #extract top x% (where x = 0.8) TIC spectra, groups fragments within a given tolerance (0.05 Da)  #This step aggregates the top 80% TIC spectra from step2 and calculates the fragment frequencies l3 = call_aggregate(l2$sps_top_tic_2, 0.05, folder_path)   #This step labels the individual spectrum with frequencies learnt from Step 3 l4 = label_individual_spectrum(l3, folder_path, 0.05)  #This step removed fragments with frequencies below the given threshold (denoising step) l5 = generate_denoised_spectra(l4, folder_path, ion_mode = "pos")

what: Tuning the optimal recurrence frequency parameter
title: DuReS
text: DuReS provides users ability determine optimal frequency cutoff denoising MS/MS spectra. detailed walkthrough available example analysis using open-source experimental tandem mass spectrometry dataset .

title: DuReS
text: DuReS includes curated reference library built 11 publicly available MS/MS datasets, comprising: 1,259,372 unique spectra 356,330 unique compounds Coverage across positive negative ionization modes Redundant entries removed using SPLASH keys (see Supporting Information, Section 3 main manuscript) processed positive negative library spectra available . Users may choose install GIT LFS using files automated manner (see vigentte titled Parameter Tuning may directly upload files link package directory /inst/extdata/. Experimental denoised spectra matched reference library using following scoring function: : - Modified Dot Product measures spectral similarity - NMF = Number Matching Fragments addition Matching Score, DuReS reports: - Forward Reverse Dot Products - Fragment Matching Ratio (FMR) - Number matched fragments - Reference compound identifiers ensure high-confidence annotations: - Matches fewer 2 fragments dot products < 0.25 filtered - Annotations must occur ≥30% replicate spectra parameters fully tunable, spectral matching algorithm integrated DuReS.
